newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Leading Belgian socialist denies murder case role.
newsitem.headline: Leading Belgian socialist denies murder case role.

text.p: Guy Mathot, a former high-living socialist minister, vehemently denied on Friday any part in the mafia-style murder of fellow Belgian socialist and ex-minister Andre Cools in 1991.

Mathot, who served as national budget minister and in regional government but was forced to resign over a bribes scandal triggered by the Cools affair, denounced the allegation by an anonymous witness to police in the eastern city of Liege.

The witness recently told investigators how two Tunisian hitmen were recruited in Sicily to gun down Cools and his girlfriend. The breakthrough shocked a country still reeling from separate revelations about a murderous paedophile gang.
"It is astonishing that there is an anonymous witness who comes forward five years later who creates...such suspicion," Mathot told Belgian RTBF television.
"Once I know the identity of this person I will take the necessary measures," he added.
The witness told police Mathot was one of three Belgian politicians who had put out a contract on Cools.
Mathot said he would cooperate with investigators.
"I ask to be heard but I will not have much to say...I am absolutely and completely a stranger to all of this, from (this case) to Agusta," he added.

Mathot lost his job as minister in the Walloon region early in 1994 over his alleged role in an orders-for-bribes scandal involving Italian helicopter maker Agusta, which came to light as a result of investigations into the Cools murder.
Mathot was described as the contact person between Agusta and the francophone Socialist Party (PS). Agusta has always denied any involvement.
In elections in May 1995, Mathot was re-elected to the regional Walloon parliament.

NATO Secretary General Willy Claes -- economics minister at the time of the Agusta orders -- was a promiment victim of Agusta scandal, which also cost three other ministers their jobs and caused the suicide of a top general.

Details of the Cools case have been emerging since last weekend and police have arrested six people, including Alain van der Biest, a former regional and federal PS minister and mayor of a Liege suburb.
Van der Biest, named by the anonymous informer, has been charged with the murder of Cools but has denied any involvment in the killing.
Van der Biest was also linked to the Cools slaying by his former private secretary Richard Taxquet, also under arrest.

Police said on Friday ballistics experts had confirmed the 7.65 mm pistol fished out of a Liege river on Sunday was the weapon used to murder Cools in the car park of his girlfriend's apartment block.
One of the six arrested, Domenico Castellino, had led police to the canal where he said the killers had dumped the gun.
Bullets still in the Belgian-made gun and those found in Cools's body had been easy to match since they were relatively rare. The ammunition was custom-made in Austria for German police.
